text.p: Programming expenses at Tele-Communications Inc's cable unit, excluding acquisitions, rose 24.2 percent in the fourth quarter over the prior year, executives said on Monday.

Total programming expenses rose 39.5 percent. Programming has outpaced revenue growth, but the senior vice president for finance Bernard Schotters told a teleconfernce call some changes will be made that will "incentivize us."
Earlier TCI Communications, the cable subsidairy, said preliminary fourth quarter revenue rose to $1.620 billion from $1.315 billion in the year-ago period.
The company also expects capital spending in 1997 to be around $750 million, compared with $1.7 billion in 1996.
But the 1996 figure included about $300 million for its satellite business, which was spun off in December.
The 1997 figure includes about the same amount for maintenance, about $240 million. The remaining $500 million will be spent on rebuilds and upgrades.
TCI has implemented a cost-cutting program that included layoffs in December.
No additional charges are expected from the layoffs.
